features.practice: Useful for YAML editor highlighting on later slides; never substitute it for the opening headmatter.
Generate and inspect the PDF with the web build; use an explicit URL when supplying an externally produced PDF.
Localize critical remote media and fonts; a service worker does not make arbitrary third-party URLs offline-safe.
Choose the canvas with the theme before laying out slides; do not change it late to conceal overflow.
Keep click cues in long notes synchronized with the actual click choreography and rehearse both forward and backward.
Use line numbers only when referring to lines; match startLine when displaying an excerpt from a file.
Prefer a shorter excerpt or split; a scrollable code block is a workshop aid, not permission for unreadable dense slides.
Enable Comark first; use tabs for equivalent alternatives, not for content the audience must compare side by side.
Opt in intentionally; keep Markdown readable and test any MDC/Comark examples copied from older documentation.
Use directional styles for continuity; always inspect backward navigation and reduced-motion behavior.
Author explicit dragPos values for deterministic exports; never make dragging the only way to obtain meaning.
Rehearse pen/touch mode, persistence, and synchronization; clean rehearsal annotations before recording or export.
Eject only when owning the theme copy is justified; a small local layout/style is cheaper to maintain.
Predict which file wins before overriding imported content; validate flattened slide numbering and title references.
Prefer per-slide layers for export-correct footers; global navigation-state layers need --per-slide export testing.
Use one coherent icon family, pin its package, give meaningful icons names/labels, and do not substitute icons for a clear visual idea.
Import tested source rather than duplicating it; keep ranges stable with region comments and use correct filename/language metadata.
Split along narrative chapters, not arbitrary editor convenience; recursively validate imported files and link numbering after edits.
Explain equations in speech and use KaTeX-supported syntax; inspect editable-PPTX raster fallbacks and non-Latin fonts.
Align highlight stages with spoken reasoning; avoid highlight changes with no visible explanation or accidental extra clicks.
Use structured edits when helpful but still review diffs, rebuild, and visually inspect; disable the HTTP endpoint on untrusted networks.
Simplify graphs before styling them; check light/dark contrast, label sizes, export rendering, and a textual explanation.
Reserve editor weight for actual live editing; a static Shiki block is faster and more faithful for read-only code.
Use only trusted code: the built-in browser runner is unsandboxed. Prepare a static output fallback and explicit Run action for critical demos.
Development only: writing saves to source files. Back up work and never enable a public write-capable demo.
Check replacement scope, typography, and correct pronunciation with a fluent speaker; not a substitute for language review.
Use an absolute public image URL in production, verify preview cards, and pin a generated image when CI font environments differ.
Treat the default renderer as a network and privacy dependency; self-host or bundle a proven image for offline/critical talks.
Format after source edits, review semantic diff and notes; do not assume formatting validates Vue/YAML or rendered layout.
Install the optional plugin, build, load once online, wait for Ready offline, then test the actual deck with network disabled.
Obtain consent, check permissions/audio/storage, and make a short test recording before the real presentation.
Bind deliberately and protect presenter mode; a password/tunnel is not justification to expose secrets or dev-only write tools publicly.
Use hand-drawn emphasis selectively; bind clicks correctly and inspect mark dimensions during backward/export states.
Set accurate title, description, canonical URL, and social image; remove private speaker notes from a public build separately.
Use small traceable edits and identical context lines; test every state, backward navigation, final code, and export without clicks.
Convenient for live source edits, not a visual QA substitute; keep development write access away from public deployments.
Clean up listeners/timers and check active-slide state; do not start expensive work for every preloaded slide.
Scope intentional one-off slide treatments; use reusable local layouts/tokens for repeated patterns and keep presenter CSS unaffected.
Use named slots exactly as the selected layout defines them; inspect nested Markdown and missing/extra slots in the browser.
Set duration after rehearsal, not aspiration; retain a Q&A/time buffer and verify countdown behavior on the presenter display.
Use for intentional miniature/diagram scaling, not to rescue overflowing body text; inspect layout box versus transformed visuals.
Use type information when it teaches something; pin TypeScript, resolve imports, and inspect hover-only information alternatives for exports.
Use visual/navigation editor tools when available; a preview is not a substitute for production build/export validation.
Use sparingly for a slide with intrinsically different density; enforce a readable minimum rather than hiding too much content with zoom.
